text:
Maria: Heads-up — instrumenting LLM requests in OTLP. We have a bunch of ad-hoc span names and dashboards are fragmented. We need a short, low-cardinality naming + attribute spec. Opinions?

Kevin: +1. My quick proposal: span name = `llm.request` (root). Attributes: model, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit, route_id, rollout_variant. No raw prompt text in attributes.

Jade: I lean toward `inference.call` to match other RPC spans, but `llm.request` is fine if we standardize. Also: add `redwood.request.type` (chat/generate/embed/rerank).

Samir: We should follow OTel semantic conventions where possible and put custom LLM attrs under a `redwood.` prefix to avoid collisions. Suggested set (low-cardinality unless noted):
- `redwood.model.name`
- `redwood.model.version`
- `redwood.model.quantization` (e.g., fp16/int8)
- `redwood.request.type` (chat|generate|embed|rerank)
- `redwood.tokens.input` (int)
- `redwood.tokens.output` (int)
- `redwood.cache.hit` (bool)
- `redwood.cache.type` (prefix|kv)
- `redwood.batch.size` (int)
- `redwood.route.id`
- `redwood.rollout.variant`

Ashley: Compliance note — we can't export raw prompts to external exporters. Solution: only export token counts and `redwood.prompt.hash` (sha256 truncated) when allowed. Mark privacy level with `redwood.privacy.level` = `redacted|hashed|full`. Default = `redacted`.

Maria: For KV/prefix cache metrics, prefer counts over booleans: `redwood.kv_cache.hits` (int) and `redwood.kv_cache.lookups`. Also consider `redwood.kv_cache.hit_ratio` (float).

Kevin: On span naming hierarchy: root `llm.request` -> child spans like `llm.cache.lookup`, `llm.model.decode`, `llm.output.postprocess`. That makes flamegraphs and p99 attribution easier.

Jade: Exporter concerns: many backends struggle with high-cardinality attrs. We must ban user-specific values (user_id, prompt_hash if unique) or sample+hash them. Recommend scrubber at the gateway that: drops/obfuscates PII, enforces an allowlist of attribute keys, and truncates long strings.

Samir: Implementation notes: SDKs add resource attributes: `service.name=redwood-inference`, `deployment.environment`, `cloud.zone`. The per-request attrs above go on the span. For retention defaults I propose: full traces retained 90d, aggregate metrics 365d, configurable per-customer.

Ashley: Also add `redwood.sample.reason` (e.g., "error", "debug", "slow_path") and `redwood.privacy.level` as mentioned so downstream teams know what data they can use.

Maria: Action items: 1) write a short spec doc with the canonical span name and attribute list, 2) add a gateway lint that enforces names/allowed attrs, 3) Samir to PR an exporter scrubber + config for retention/sampling, 4) Kevin to update dashboards to query `llm.request` spans.

Kevin: I'll prototype the dashboard queries tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Samir: I'll open the OTLP exporter PR with a scrubber that drops prompt text and truncates hashes by default. Also adding a config flag `exporter.allow_prompt_export=true` guarded by legal review.

Jade: Minor: span durations carry latency; add `redwood.compute.gpu_type` or `redwood.hardware.class` (g4dn/p4d/etc) but keep it low-cardinality.

Maria: Example minimal span attributes (for the spec) — please review and call out anything missing:

```json
{
  "name": "llm.request",
  "attributes": {
    "redwood.model.name": "redwood-7b",
    "redwood.model.version": "v2",
    "redwood.request.type": "chat",
    "redwood.tokens.input": 24,
    "redwood.tokens.output": 128,
    "redwood.cache.hit": false,
    "redwood.batch.size": 1,
    "redwood.rollout.variant": "canary-3",
    "redwood.privacy.level": "redacted"
  }
}
```

Ashley: LGTM. Please ensure the spec calls out which attrs are allowed to be high-cardinality (only `redwood.rollout.variant`?) and that `redwood.prompt.hash` is always truncated and opt-in.

Maria: OK — I'll draft the spec and add the lint rules. Thanks everyone.

Kevin: Thanks — will wait for the PRs.

Samir: Opening PRs now.

Jade: Nice, feel free to @channel when the spec is up for review.
